sentence_stem: Before you travel abroad, you have to
correct_completion: check that your passport is still valid.
full_sentence: Before you travel abroad, you have to check that your passport is still valid.
acceptable_variants: make sure your visa has not expired.
renew your documents if they are out of date.

options.text: wear a suit on the plane.
options.why_wrong: Wearing a suit is not a requirement for travel, so it does not express a logical obligation for this situation.

options.text: check that your passport is still valid.

options.why_wrong: This is not a logical requirement before traveling abroad, so it does not complete the obligation the stem introduces.

options.text: bring your bicycle to the hotel.
options.why_wrong: This is not a general requirement for travel abroad, so it does not fit the meaning of 'have to' here.

explanation: 'Have to' expresses a necessity, so the completion must describe something a traveler is actually obliged to do. Spanish speakers may confuse this with 'must', but both forms express obligation in this context.
translation: Antes de viajar al extranjero, tienes que comprobar que tu pasaporte sigue siendo válido.
